battlecards.why_selected: Best overall economics – $297K annual rebate plus $22K in front-end price reductions under a national program while retaining existing Carrier product ecosystem.
battlecards.contract_terms: National price list signed 9/25/2025; pricing held until written notice; annual volume rebate starting at 15% of net purchases; term aligned to calendar year with mutual renewal option.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Multi-OEM benchmark data and threat to shift $2M spend created pressure for price concessions.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Recognized brand, broad equipment portfolio, strong distributor support network.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Historically inconsistent local pricing; limited transparency on parts pricing.
battlecards.switching_costs: High – technician familiarity, installed base warranties, parts inventory.
battlecards.notes: Q3 rebate true-up under review could raise annual rebate to $406K.

battlecards.why_selected: Direct OEM agreement lifted rebate from 6.5% to 8% and standardized national pricing with no distributor mark-up.
battlecards.contract_terms: Consolidator Incentive Agreement effective 1/1/2026; 1-year term with renewal; rebates paid on net purchases across all Dealer Partners; new acquisitions can be added via exhibit.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregated volume across five business units to qualify for higher rebate tier; credible threat to divert spend to competing OEMs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Competitive rebate ladder, flexibility to add future acquisitions, strong distributor fulfillment network.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Still reliant on distributors for product flow; limited direct influence on front-end prices.
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate – product familiarity but alternatives readily available.
battlecards.notes: Front-end pricing parity still being validated; savings currently driven by rebate delta.

battlecards.why_selected: Agreed to 16% rebate on all dollars spent (~$441K) with minimal operational disruption.
battlecards.contract_terms: National rebate program – 16% tier for $1M–$8M spend; rebates paid quarterly; signing bonus under discussion.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Displayed unfavorable price gaps on like-for-like SKUs versus Daikin and Carrier, threatening to redirect volume.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Large installed base, reliable lead times, generous rebate percentage.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher front-end pricing than peers; limited flexibility on key SKUs.
battlecards.switching_costs: High – equipment compatibility and technician training.
battlecards.notes: Further front-end pricing improvements under review; signing bonus expected between $50-200K.

battlecards.why_selected: Enhanced ECM rebate (2% base + 5% growth) delivered savings without switching suppliers.
battlecards.contract_terms: Annual ECM rebate program reviewed each year; no minimum purchase commitment.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Potential to shift ECM parts to Ferguson created pressure for higher rebate.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Broad ECM inventory, existing logistics network.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Declined full national HVAC program; limited price concessions beyond rebate.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low-moderate – parts interchangeable but would require supplier onboarding.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided lowest Round-2 pricing and agreed to national MOU with 2% early-pay discount.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU effective 1/1/2026-12/31/2026; 30-day notice for manufacturer-validated price increases; Net-30 terms with 2% discount if paid by 10th.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: SKU-level competitive bid across four incumbents with option for exclusive award.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Aggressive pricing on commodity SKUs; national distribution footprint.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Quoted only 14% of requested SKUs; potential regional service gaps.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low – products largely interchangeable; requires onboarding and catalog alignment.
battlecards.notes: Preferred supplier designation pending final signature.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Round-2 pricing still above R.E. Michel; produced negative savings on key SKUs.
battlecards.contract_terms: Draft MOU prepared but not executed.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Incumbent position but could not match competitor pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Largest SKU coverage of incumbents; established relationships.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Higher pricing; slow response on pricing transparency.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low – comparable products available from competitors.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Failed to deliver material savings; negative $7K in Round-2 unit price analysis.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Incumbent volume but underperformed on pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Quoted widest SKU list (38% of RFQ).

battlecards.why_not_selected: Limited SKU overlap and higher unit prices; quoted only 9% of SKUs.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Niche IAQ products gave limited leverage.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low – IAQ products can be sourced elsewhere.

battlecards.why_selected: Rampart GPO pricing yielded 43% savings and allowed single national provider.
battlecards.contract_terms: GPO agreement; rollout 3-4 months; rental program with standardized rates across BUs.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to migrate 83% of volume from Cintas to Unifirst; aggregated headcount across brands.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Competitive GPO rates, national footprint, existing service at two BUs.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Inventory transition time, limited presence in some micro-markets.
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate – coordination of garment returns and new sizing.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Could not match Unifirst GPO pricing; continued would forgo 43% savings.
battlecards.contract_terms: Existing location-level agreements allowed termination with notice.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Large incumbent share but pricing above market benchmarks.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Established service routes, responsive account teams.
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate – need to handle garment return logistics.

summary.skipped_reason: No simple-spend-only suppliers in complex categories
